Ticket clocks run in business hours, supervisors see their own teams, and escalation tells people instead of moving tickets.

GOOD TO KNOW

Tickets in business hours: a ticket's due times count only open time, from its contract tier's hours, else its queue's opening hours, else the new Business hours for tickets (Ticket settings), else round the clock. Waits on the customer, the owner's warning and reminder, the Tickets and Conversations reports, the live monitor and wallboards count the same way. Recalculate due times (Ticket settings, administrators) puts this right for recent tickets, after a count first: breaches and automatic escalations made only by nights and weekends are undone, each explained on the ticket.

Escalation is a notice, not a move: an escalated ticket always stays with its agent. The agent and the team leader are told first (supervisors only when the team has no leader); if it is still open after the second-level hours, the team's supervisors are told. Setting a ticket's status to Escalated by hand now tells the same people.

Supervisors see their own teams: a team member can now be a Member, Team leader or Supervisor. A supervisor named on teams sees and acts on only those teams' agents, queues and tickets on the floor, the live monitor and the real-time view; one named on no team still sees everyone, and administrators always do.

Missed calls: every unanswered inbound call is now recorded and listed, with or without a missed-call campaign; a campaign set up later takes calls missed in the last 24 hours. The list missed callers join can be any list, or a new one made there.

The nightly 04:00 restart of the call servers no longer sends emails; only a server still down 10 minutes into its restart is reported.

FOR AGENTS

Waiting on internal feedback: a new ticket status beside Waiting on the customer, with who you are waiting on. It stops the clock the same way, is never closed by itself, is not ended by the customer writing, and a reply from where the ticket was forwarded puts it back in progress.

Attach file: files on a ticket's reply go to the customer with the email and stay on the ticket.

Ticket messages first: a ticket's emails and messages are the first thing on it, above the timeline.

Calls you place: you hear the customer's line ring (or the network's own tones and announcements) until they answer. When Call is grey because the last call still needs its outcome, the desk says so beside it.

Email reactions: a customer's reaction in Outlook (a thumbs up) shows on the conversation as a reaction and is no longer answered with an automatic reply.

FOR SUPERVISORS

New reports: inbound and outbound calls by 15, 30 or 60 minutes; abandoned calls in detail (by hour, why and how long callers waited); agent time detail (ready, talk, wrap-up, parked and paused by each reason, adding up to logged-in time); pause reasons; agent conversion; list performance and penetration; hangup causes (with each call's carrier for platform operators); calls by number dialled in; and call flow paths.

Drill-down: a count in the call reports opens the calls behind it, each with a link to its timeline.

Excel: every report exports as Excel as well as CSV, and scheduled reports can attach Excel. Scheduled reports offer every filter a report takes.

My reports: build your own report from calls, tickets, conversations, agent time or leads, with rows and columns, figures and filters; save it, share it with everyone or chosen roles, export, schedule and drill into it.

Transcripts: select all and export the chosen transcripts as one ZIP of PDFs.

FOR ADMINISTRATORS

Outcomes: a new Counts as a sale tick, used by the sales figures (outcomes named SALE are ticked already).

Rename: campaigns and call flows can be renamed, and Duplicate asks for the copy's name.

Campaigns"}
